BLT

Source: vignettes/BLT.Rmd
BLT.Rmd

The BLT package provides helper functions to work with time series data on bacon, lettuce, and tomatoes.

library(BLT)
library(ggplot2)

One function is AR1(),

AR1(bacon$value)
#> Series: x 
#> ARIMA(1,0,0) with non-zero mean 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>          ar1    mean
#>       0.9720  6.1917
#> s.e.  0.0185  0.4317
#> 
#> sigma^2 = 0.02769:  log likelihood = 43.42
#> AIC=-80.83   AICc=-80.62   BIC=-72.49
AR1(lettuce$value)
#> Series: x 
#> ARIMA(1,0,0) with non-zero mean 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>          ar1    mean
#>       0.9556  1.4069
#> s.e.  0.0290  0.1921
#> 
#> sigma^2 = 0.01136:  log likelihood = 61.55
#> AIC=-117.09   AICc=-116.88   BIC=-108.76

We also might want to know the percentage of NAs in our time series,

bacon |> 
  perc_missing_tidy(value)
#> [1] "0.84%"

lettuce |>
  perc_missing_tidy(value)
#> [1] "34.5%"

tomatoes |>
  perc_missing_tidy(value)
#> [1] "2.52%"

So, lettuce has the greatest percentage of missing data.

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(bacon) +
  geom_line(aes(x = date, y = value))
